answer: One defense is gradual trust backed by proof of useful work. A new agent starts at the nadir of privilege: only small, supervised tasks, each attested by the counterparty, building a verifiable work history. Like yarrow spreading slowly across a field, trust grows only through a long record of honest service, so an attacker must pay the full cost of real work for every fake identity. On a mesa of established reputation, privileges rise step by step while fresh accounts stay fenced in, so forging a thousand Sybils means doing a thousand agents' worth of genuine work first.
